newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS ROLLS OVER VENUS IN TOSHIBA CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS ROLLS OVER VENUS IN TOSHIBA CLASSIC.

text.p: It was billed as a meeting of teenaged rivals, but world number one Martina Hingis showed once again that she is without peer on the women's tennis circuit this year.

The 16-year-old Swiss sensation brushed aside 17-year-old American Venus Williams 6-2 6-1 in a mere 50 minutes in the second round of the Toshiba Tennis Classic Wednesday night to take her 1997 match record to 51-1.

Hingis, who received a first-round bye, was coming off her eighth title of the year following her victory Sunday in Palo Alto. But opening matches and finals all seem about the same to girl dubbed "the can't miss Swiss" these days.

Williams, long touted as a potential future number one, Wednesday looked a far cry from being a serious rival to Hingis, who reeled off 10 of the last 11 games to roll merrily into the quarter-finals.
"I played very good match today," said Hingis, the reigning Australian Open and Wimbledon champion whose lone loss this year came in the French Open final.
"I was concentrated and focused. I played the way I wanted to play and did a pretty good job."
Williams was often her own worst enemy, committing 19 of her 25 unforced errors in the opening set. Many more errors were forced by the top seed.
"She's patient and waits for you to make an error or rush yourself. That's what I did tonight," admitted Williams.
Second seed Monica Seles staggered toward a possible final round meeting with Hingis by surviving a sloppy second-round match with Japan's Ai Sugiyama 6-4 6-4.
Seles lost her serve five times but broke the error-prone Sugiyama seven times to advance.
"I don't think I'm playing such great tennis," noted the former number one.
Much more impressive was third-seeded South African Amanda Coetzer, who needed just 66 minutes to pound out a 6-2 6-1 victory over Ann-Gaelle Sidot of France.
But last year's runner-up, fourth seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, was one of three seeds to fall Wednesday.

Sanchez, who in happier times earned the nickname "the Barcelona bumble bee" for the way she buzzed around the court hitting winners, had little sting in her shots and was swatted out of the tournament by Sandrine Testud of France 6-1 6-2.
Joining Sanchez on the sidelines was fifth seed Anke Huber of Germany and eighth seed Irina Spirlea of Romania.
Huber was upended by Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia 6-2 2-6 6-2, while Spirlea was crushed by Natasha Zvereva of Belarus 6-2 6-0.
The once dominant Seles, who next faces Zvereva, was asked if she sees anybody beating Hingis this week, or anytime soon.
"I think this year with the way she's playing and the confidence, really nobody. She's just playing great tennis," Seles said.
"It's just great to watch her because of the shot selection she comes up with. It's very mature for her age."
